classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the requested angle cannot be found directly, calculate both possible values of B, validate them, and use each to find theta.

content.prompt: Find the value(s) of $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 25, left column immediately above additional practice
spec.description: Wide unshaded triangle ABC, with A and B on the horizontal base and C above it. AC is labelled 20, BC is labelled 17, angle A is 20 degrees and angle C is theta. Ordinary edges, labels and angle marks are black.
spec.mathematics: Coordinates derive from AC:BC = 20:17 and angle A = 20 degrees, using the wide triangle shown in the source. Coordinates are construction data, not additional student givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the printed givens and theta are visible; neither possible answer is supplied.

inlines.text: Find both possible values of angle B using the sine rule, then subtract each from 160°.

answer.worked:
Using the sine rule,
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{\sin B}{20}&=\frac{\sin20^\circ}{17}\\
\sin B&=\frac{20\sin20^\circ}{17}\\
B&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{20\sin20^\circ}{17}\right)\text{ or }180^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{20\sin20^\circ}{17}\right)\\
B&\approx23.726838^\circ\text{ or }156.273162^\circ
\end{align*}$$
Both candidates satisfy $20^\circ+B<180^\circ$, so both triangles are possible.
$$\begin{align*}
\theta&=180^\circ-20^\circ-B\\
\theta&\approx136.273162^\circ\text{ or }3.726838^\circ
\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $\theta\approx136^\circ$ or $4^\circ$, to the nearest degree.
